VeraVox 1.5.0

A queue you can take back, multiple selection and a Columns view in the Library, a Dynamic Range report to export, and a good number of fixes. Your library, queues, saved playlists and settings are untouched, except for the Dynamic Range figures: see below.

The queue

  • Playing from the Library still replaces the queue, but the old one is no longer lost: a notice offers Restore for a few seconds, and Restore Previous Queue in the Queue's ⋯ menu brings it back for the rest of the session, on the Web Remote too.
  • Option-click a track's play icon, or choose Play Now, Keep Queue, to play it without replacing the queue. New Playlist… in the right-click menu of a track, an album or an artist makes a saved playlist directly.
  • With Shuffle on, a queue starts from a random track, or from the one you pick, and the shuffled order follows the queue as you change it. At the end of the queue, Play starts it again.

The Library

  • Select several tracks or albums with click, ⌘-click, ⇧-click and ⌘A, then right-click to play, queue, add to a playlist, favourite, rate or analyse them all at once. Esc steps back one level at a time.
  • On the Artists tab, a large enough window offers a Columns layout: artists and albums side by side, tracks below. An artist can also show all of their tracks in one sortable list.
  • Back and Forward in the Library: from the Library menu (⌘[ and ⌘]), with ⌘← and ⌘→, with the mouse's side buttons, or with a two-finger swipe when Swipe between pages is set that way in System Settings.
  • Track lists are tidier: durations never wrap, DR and LRA line up in columns, a narrow pane leaves more room to the title, and every row's right-click menu sets a favourite or a rating.
  • Accented and non-Latin titles read correctly in more files, and Smart Playlist text rules ignore accents and case. Rebuild This Folder… in the Folder Manager refreshes files already in the library.

Dynamic Range

  • The DR value follows the published measurement procedure in every detail and matches the reference meters and the community DR database track for track. To keep every figure consistent, values computed by earlier versions are cleared once, at the first launch. To measure again, right-click an album and choose Compute Dynamic Range: one album at a time, whenever you like. Tools ▸ Analyze Library Dynamic Range… measures the whole library in one pass, which takes a long time on a large library, and longer from a network share or a NAS.
  • The DR shown on an album is the official album value, the rounded average of its tracks, with the minimum and maximum in the tooltip.
  • Export an album's Dynamic Range report as a PDF or a text log, from the album's right-click menu or from Track Info. It is proposed in the album's own folder, where the Booklet opens it. The analysis also measures RMS.

Other fixes

  • Gapless playback between tracks of different formats, in single-file CUE albums and in a queue restored at launch; a change to the queue midway through a track now reaches the track that follows.
  • Single-file CUE albums show each track's own duration and measurements.
  • Playback from a network share or a NAS starts faster and is steadier on the first listen.
  • Some mono and floating-point files, and some multichannel files on shared outputs, now play as they should.
  • Stop, Play and Pause respond the same way from every control, Control Center and headphones included.
  • More reliable track changes with network renderers and in UPnP Renderer Mode.
  • Smaller fixes to Choose Cover with many images, to album headers opened from the player, and to the Web Remote's menus and scrolling on iPhone and iPad.

Most of the improvements above began with someone taking the time to write in and describe what they saw.

VeraVox 1.4.0

A large update: a cover of your choosing, a text size for the whole interface, album favourites, text documents in the Booklet, the Signal Path on the Web Remote, and corrections in the Library, on HDMI outputs and in the Signal Generator. Your library, queues, saved playlists and settings are untouched. The first library update after installing takes a little longer than usual; the reason is under The Library.

Covers

  • You choose which image is the cover of an album, or of one disc of a box set: right-click the cover in the player or the mini player, an album in the Library or a disc header, and pick any image found in the album's folders or any image file on disk. VeraVox shows it everywhere it shows a cover, the Web Remote, the macOS Now Playing display and a Tuneshine included. Automatic brings back the cover your files give. Your files and folders are never written.
  • A box set whose files carry two covers no longer needs the tag-order trick: choose the disc's cover for playback and keep the box on the album's tile.
  • Tools ▸ Cover Window (⌘⌥C) shows the current cover large while you listen; the arrow keys leaf through the album's images.

Text size

  • Settings has a Text Size card with four steps: Small, Default, Large and Larger. Every window follows at once and nothing is clipped, because rows, columns and popovers grow with the text. If you change nothing, nothing changes. The instrument panels and the Mini Player keep their own lettering; the Help window keeps its own zoom on top.

The Library

  • A whole album goes into Favorites, and out, with one click: right-click one or more covers, use the ♥ in the album's header, or the heart in the album header of the Web Remote. Hearts and stars in the lists now sit in one column, whatever the figures beside them.
  • The scroll bar is back at the right edge, where every Mac window puts it, with the A-Z index just inside.
  • Text files kept beside the music (.txt notes, a .md readme, a release .nfo) join the Booklet after the PDFs, on the Mac and on the Web Remote: an album with notes and no PDF gets the book badge, and a text file opens in a monospaced pane with search and zoom. Per-track lyrics files stay out. After installing, the first library update re-checks every folder once so the badges appear.
  • Three tag corrections. WAV files written by a TagLib-based tag editor now sort by their Sort Artist and Sort Album Artist tags, as FLAC and AIFF already did. Compilations credited to Various Artists sort under V even when every track carries its own performer's sort tag. AIFF and MP3 files tagged in Music, or in iTunes before it, arrive with album artist, track numbers, year, genre, composer and compilation flag, so those compilations stay together. Files already in the library take the corrections after Rebuild This Folder in the Folder Manager, since an ordinary update does not re-read files that have not changed.

Playback and devices

  • An HDMI or optical output whose only exclusive formats are the Dolby and DTS bitstream carriers used to show as Exclusive Ready, and with Exclusive Mode on a multichannel file above 48 kHz could come out as loud distortion. Such an output now shows as Shared Output, Exclusive is not offered on it, and every file takes the shared path that already played cleanly; the DAC Diagnostic panel lists those carriers as Encoded. If your receiver is connected this way, the new label is the correction, not a loss.
  • With Exclusive Mode on, a multichannel file on a device that can carry every channel but has exclusive formats for stereo only used to start in exclusive stereo without asking, surrounds lost. VeraVox now asks and offers Play All Channels (Shared Output) first; Play L/R Only remains. Stereo DACs and virtual devices are not affected.
  • If you run a convolver or room correction after VeraVox, the Signal Path used to say High Quality for the handoff to your virtual device. It now says Bit-Perfect Handoff when the device runs at the file's rate, and the popover explains that what comes after the device is yours. It stays High Quality, with the conversion step in view, when the device resamples or the source is DSD.

Signal Generator

  • While the generator plays, the player shows a Signal Generator card with the output device, the path and the format badge with the Signal Path LED, and the drawer has a DEVICE line reading HOG, SHARED or FAILED. Before, the player showed its empty face and the drawer never said where the signal was going.
  • The generator stops together with the sound: Stop from anywhere, or a track started from the queue, switches it off, where before the drawer and the Vectorscope kept drawing a figure that was no longer there. The queue stays neutral while it plays, and the Web Remote says so instead of showing the previous track.
  • In the Modern theme the RATE and DEPTH menus have a readable chevron, RESET, REF 0dB and IMPULSE respond, the bezel keeps its round corners with the drawer open, and the DAC Diagnostic panel's ALL PHYSICAL FORMATS row shows the triangle that opens it.

Web Remote

  • The format badge carries the same coloured Signal Path LED as the Mac; tapping it opens the full chain, from the source file to the output device, with the same label and steps. In the Output tab, local devices show their tier: Exclusive Ready, Shared Output or Lossy.
  • The Settings tab reads like the rest of VeraVox: devices in grouped panels with the picker's LED and a tick on the active output, switches for Composer, Year and Group by Work, two equal segmented controls for Theme and Waveform. Nothing changes in what the settings do.
  • When nothing is playing, Now Playing shows the VeraVox mark in the artwork frame with a hint to pick a track. The album, disc, composer and device names under the title are as readable as the artist's, in both themes and under any cover.
  • On an iPad held in landscape, the Playing tab puts the cover on the left and the title, waveform and controls on the right, nothing hidden under the tab bar. The Library ends with the same status line the Mac shows: albums, tracks and total playing time of what the tab lists.

Most of the improvements above began with someone taking the time to write in and describe what they saw.

VeraVox 1.3.0

A wide update: playback settings, the queue, the Library drawer, and a long list of smaller things. Your library, queues, saved playlists and settings are untouched, and there is nothing you need to do.

Playback

  • Bit Depth in Settings is now a choice of three: Match source, Prefer 24-bit (the default, and what VeraVox has always done) and Maximum. With Match source a 16-bit file reaches the DAC as 16 bits, and a DAC that displays its input depth shows the file's. If you had Max Bit Depth switched on you will find Maximum selected; if you change nothing, nothing changes.
  • An amber line under the picker may say that two of the settings deliver the same depth on your DAC, at some sample rates or at all, even when the DAC's format list shows that depth. It is not a fault. What counts is not only which depths a DAC lists but how each one is laid out: VeraVox keeps every sample in a 32-bit word, Prefer 24-bit and Maximum take only the formats that word is copied into as it is, and a 24-bit format packed into three bytes is not one of them, so on such a DAC both deliver 32 bits. Match source is the one setting that repacks to reach the file's exact depth, and where the DAC has no 16-bit format it lands where Prefer 24-bit does. In every case your bits travel unmodified, with zeros below them when the word is wider: bit-perfect either way. The line only tells you in advance which settings your DAC cannot tell apart.
  • A 24-bit ALAC on a DAC that offers only 16-bit exclusive formats at that rate used to go out truncated under the Bit-Perfect label. It now takes the Shared path and says so. Nothing changes for any other file.
  • Audio interfaces with no 2-channel output format, as most recording interfaces are, could not play FLAC, WavPack and RF64 files: noise in Exclusive, several times too fast in Shared. They play normally on both paths now; in Exclusive the Signal Path shows Enhanced with a Format Conversion step.
  • The DAC Diagnostic panel's table of physical formats gains a Packing column, and the tag beside the format says when the Bit Depth choice made no difference at that rate.

The queue

  • Each row reads like a Library row: artist and album under the title, a short format badge such as 24/96 or DSD64, the duration in a straight column, and the title with all the room at every width. Composer and year follow the same Settings switch as the Library.
  • The heart and the stars are live, as in Now Playing. A title that does not fit unfolds whole when you rest the pointer on it.
  • Right-click a row: Play, Play Next, Move to Top, Move to End, Remove from Queue, Favorites and Rating, Add to Saved Playlist, Show in Library, Get Info, Show in Finder. With several rows selected it acts on all of them and says how many.
  • The Web Remote's queue shows the album and the same short badge.

The Library and its drawer

  • The Library comes back on the tab you were using: after a relaunch, after ⌘L, and after moving it between the drawer and its own window.
  • The drawer can be as wide as the window allows. The album grid shows as many columns as fit at your cover size, and the zoom slider appears in the drawer's status bar once there is room for it. At the usual widths nothing changes.
  • The drawer can no longer be squeezed until its title and search field are cut off. If you had saved a narrower drawer, it opens at the new minimum.
  • The summary line under the Library reads whole at any width, and while you search it counts what the tab is showing rather than matches hidden in genre, composer, year or comments.

Booklets and the Web Remote

  • If an album folder holds more than one PDF, you see them all: tabs above the pages on the Mac (⌃Tab and ⌃⇧Tab step through them), chips on the Web Remote. A box set with a booklet per disc lists all of them from the album page.
  • On the Web Remote, a cover you have changed updates without restarting VeraVox.

Network renderers and the diagnostic report

  • A renderer that states its service addresses in relative form, as the UPnP standard prescribes, used to appear in the picker and answer no command. It works now; renderers that already worked are untouched.
  • The diagnostic report stays readable after hours on the network: a silent device is reported once rather than every five minutes, a device announcing itself under a dozen names appears as one, a control point polling for position is one line per streak, and a Mac that cannot send multicast says so once. Nothing changes on the network or in the audio.

Backups

  • Restoring a backup made by an older VeraVox brings the library up to today's model, where before compilations could come back split, or some covers and tags missing. If you never restore a backup, nothing changes.
  • A search index that has fallen behind the library is now noticed at launch and rebuilt in the background.

Several of the improvements above began with someone taking the time to write in and describe what they saw.
